Why does fusion in a massive star stop at iron?
Fusing iron uses up energy instead of releasing it
Iron is too heavy for gravity to squeeze
The star runs out of hydrogen first
Iron is too cold to fuse

slides.reveal: Answer: A. Iron is the most tightly bound nucleus, so any reaction that changes it takes energy rather than giving it; the core loses its energy supply and collapses (slides 14 and 15; OpenStax 23.2).
